awd_titl_txt: Conference: Southern Regional Council on Statistics Summer Research Conference
awd_abstract_narration:
The 60th Summer Research Conference (SRC) and Statistics Undergraduate Research Experience (SURE) will be held in Jekyll Island, Georgia on June 9-11, 2025. The Southern Regional Council on Statistics (SRCOS) is a consortium of statistics and biostatistics programs from universities in 16 states in the Southern region. The SRC is an annual conference sponsored by the SRCOS. The purpose of the SRC is to encourage the interchange and mutual understanding of current research ideas in statistics and biostatistics, and to provide motivation and direction to further research progress. The SRC will give new researchers an opportunity to participate in the meeting and to interact closely with leaders in the field in a manner not possible at larger meetings. In addition to the graduate student participation, the 60th SRC will also include the 6th annual Statistical Undergraduate Research Experience (SURE) from June 9-11, 2025. SURE is a conference within a conference aimed to encourage the participation of undergraduate students to pursue graduate education and career opportunities in STEM fields. SURE will include events specifically for undergraduate students and undergraduate mentors, such as a panel about career opportunities in statistics, a real data analytics workshop, and a speed-mentoring session with current statistics and biostatistics graduate students.
 
The SRC is particularly valuable for graduate students, isolated statisticians, and faculty from smaller regional schools in the southern region at drivable distances without the cost of travel to distant venues. Speakers will present formal research talks with adequate time allowed for clarification, amplification, and further informal discussions in small groups.  Under the travel support provided by this award, graduate students will attend and present their research in posters to be reviewed by more experienced researchers. Participation in SURE will encourage undergraduate students to enter STEM fields, including statistics or biostatistics, and provide training to support this endeavor. The 60th SRC will strengthen the research of the statistics and biostatistics community as a whole and help bridge the gap for undergraduate students to pursue statistics or biostatistics, particularly in the sixteen states of the Southern Region. The SRCOS website can be found here: https://www.srcos.org; the SRC website can be found here: https://www.srcos.org/conference; the SURE website can be found here: https://www.srcos.org/sure.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The Summer Research Conference (SRC) is an annual research conference sponsored by the Southern Regional Council on Statistics (SRCOS). Since the inception of the SRC, the purposes of the conference are to encourage the interchange and mutual understanding of research ideas in statistics and biostatistics, and to give motivation and direction to further research progress, particularly for young researchers, in a manner not ordinarily possible at other meetings. The meeting is particularly valuable for graduate students, isolated statisticians, and faculty from smaller regional schools in the Southern Region. Each year, the location of the conference is chosen to be at a drivable distance for researchers in the Southern Region, thus affording them the opportunity to participate and interact closely with internationally known leaders in the field without the cost of travel to distant venues. Speakers present formal research talks with adequate time allowed for clarification, amplification, and further informal discussions in small groups. As such, speakers, session chairs, and discussants make themselves accessible for informal discussions of their research as well as formal presentations.

The 60th Annual Summer Research Conference (SRC) was held June 8th – 11th, 2025 in Jekyll Island, Georgia. It was co-organized by the Southern Regional Council on Statistics (SRCOS) and Emory University. More than 100 scholars from institutions across the country (Alabama to Oklahoma, the Carolinas to Missouri) participated. The website for the meeting (www.srcos.org) contains program details, abstracts, and information about conference activities. Thanks to NSF support for students, limited SRCOS funds from registrations and membership fees could be used to provide support the conference. Drs. Robert Taylor (Emeritus Faculty Member at Clemson University and American Statistical Association Fellow) and D’Arcy Mays (Executive Associate Dean for Administration and Analytics at Virginia Commonwealth University) jointly gave the 2nd annual Arnold J. Stromberg banquet lecture. Dr. Natalie Dean (Associate Professor, Department of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics, Emory University) and Dr. Michael Kosorok (W.R. Kenan, Jr. Distinguished Professor of Biostatistics, University of North Carolina) each gave keynote lectures on days 2 and 3 of the conference, respectively. The conference featured five additional stimulating invited oral sessions, featuring outstanding faculty speakers at both the senior and junior levels.

 

Within the 2025 SRC, SRCOS also held its sixth undergraduate portion of their Summer Research Conference.  Co-PIs Thompson and Hawk co-directed the program, including advertisement, planning, and implementation of the program. In total, eleven undergraduate students participated in SURE, a conference within the 2025 SRC. The students were engaged, attending sessions alongside graduate students and faculty at the SRC, but also participating in SURE-specific sessions.  These SURE-specific sessions included a graduate student perspectives panel, a career information session, a graduate student mentoring session, and a data analytics workshop.

 

After hearing information about graduate school and careers in statistics and data analytics, Co-PI Hawk led a mentoring session, where small groups including 1-2 graduate students and 1-2 undergraduate students asked and answered questions about graduate school.  In this session, many students spoke well into the allotted break time. Undergraduates were able to ask questions that they may not have had another opportunity to ask about graduate education in STEM.

 

The last SURE-specific event was a data analytics workshop led by Co-PI Thompson.  Students used publicly available Airbnb data to create both plots and geographic visualizations of the data, which they then used to identify listing characteristics related to the price and/or quality of the rental.  Students worked in both JMP and R as a group, but then explored the data further using one of these software packages based on their own preferences.  Methods and code were provided for both new and experienced programmers.  By using both types of software, the workshop was able to provide differentiated instructional opportunities to a multidisciplinary group of STEM students. To conclude the workshop, students had an opportunity to present their best data visualization to the group.

 

The NSF/R.L. Anderson Student Poster Session featured poster presentations from 34 graduate students, representing many graduate programs across the Southern Region.  Travel awards were provided by funding from the National Science Foundation, with additional support from the American Statistical Association (ASA) and SRCOS. These awards enabled students, in many cases representing programs with limited travel budgets, to experience a significant scientific conference firsthand. They interacted closely with leading researchers in the field in a manner that is not possible at larger national or international meetings (which would also be prohibitively expensive for many of these students to attend). The recipients of the M. Clinton Miller Graduate Student Poster Award were Yanyan Zhan (University of South Carolina) and Yuanyao Tan (Florida State University); the recipients of the R.L. Anderson Graduate Student Poster Award were Heranga Rathnasekara (Old Dominion University), Xin Feng (University of Texas at Dallas), and Asanka Duwage (Mississippi State University).
